cards.heading: Why bundle links
cards.body: Spanning tree blocks all but one of several parallel links between two switches. An EtherChannel bundles up to 8 active physical links into one logical port-channel interface, so STP sees a single link: all members forward, and losing one member doesn't change the topology. LACP can hold up to 8 more links in hot-standby.

cards.heading: LACP, PAgP or static
cards.body: LACP (802.3ad, open standard) uses modes active and passive. PAgP (Cisco) uses desirable and auto. Mode on forces the bundle with no negotiation at all. You can't mix protocols, and 'on' only works with 'on'. LACP is IEEE 802.3ad (now 802.1AX); PAgP is Cisco-proprietary. Active and desirable start negotiation; passive and auto only answer, so at least one side must start it.
cards.example:
active   + active/passive   → LACP
desirable + desirable/auto  → PAgP
on + on                    → static
passive + passive, auto + auto → nothing

cards.heading: Configure it
cards.body: Put the same channel-group number and mode on every member port. IOS creates the port-channel interface for you; configure trunking or VLANs on the port-channel and it's copied to the members.
cards.example:
interface range gi0/1 - 2
 channel-group 1 mode active
interface port-channel 1
 switchport mode trunk

cards.heading: Members must match
cards.body: Speed, duplex, switchport mode, access VLAN (or native VLAN and allowed list on a trunk) must be identical on every member. A port that differs is suspended. Descriptions and port numbers don't matter.

cards.heading: Verify
cards.body: show etherchannel summary lists each group, its protocol and every member with a flag: P = bundled, s = suspended, I = stand-alone, D = down. The port-channel shows SU when it's a layer 2 bundle in use.
cards.example:
Group  Port-channel  Protocol    Ports
1      Po1(SU)       LACP        Gi0/1(P)    Gi0/2(P)

cards.heading: Load balancing and layer 3 bundles
cards.body: An EtherChannel doesn't split one frame across links. It hashes addresses (MAC, IP and optionally ports) to pick one member per flow, which keeps each flow's frames in order; one big flow can't go faster than a single member. 'port-channel load-balance src-dst-ip' hashes the source and destination IPs, so one pair of hosts always uses the same link. A layer 3 EtherChannel uses 'no switchport' on the members and the port-channel, and the IP address goes on the port-channel.
cards.example:
port-channel load-balance src-dst-ip
interface range g1/0/1 - 2
 no switchport
 channel-group 2 mode active
interface port-channel 2
 no switchport
 ip address 10.0.12.1 255.255.255.252
